nat: Network Address Translation maps IP addresses in a packet header while in transit across a routing device.
ssh: Secure Shell protocol for secure remote login and other secure network services over an insecure network.
ping: Tests the reachability of a host across an Internet Protocol network and measures round-trip time.
snat: Source Network Address Translation modifies the source IP address in the IP header of outbound packets, commonly used for sharing a single public IP.
dnat: Destination Network Address Translation modifies the destination IP address of incoming packets, often used for port forwarding.
pat: Port Address Translation (or NAT overload) maps multiple private IP addresses to a single public IP address using different ports.
subnet: A logical subdivision of an IP network, allowing a network to be partitioned into smaller, manageable segments.
vlan: Virtual Local Area Network partitions a physical network into multiple logical networks for security and traffic management.
dhcp: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol automatically assigns IP addresses and network configuration parameters to devices on a network.
dns: Domain Name System translates human-friendly domain names into machine-readable IP addresses.
firewall: A network security system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined security rules.
ldap: Lightweight Directory Access Protocol used for accessing and maintaining distributed directory information services over an IP network.
tcp: Transmission Control Protocol: a connection-oriented transport protocol that provides reliable, ordered, and error-checked delivery of a stream of bytes between applications.
udp: User Datagram Protocol: a connectionless transport protocol that sends datagrams without guarantees of delivery, ordering, or duplicate protection.
icmp: Internet Control Message Protocol: used by network devices to send error messages and operational information (e.g., ping).
icmpv6: ICMP for IPv6: carries error and informational messages for IPv6, and is essential for Neighbor Discovery and SLAAC.
arp: Address Resolution Protocol: maps an IPv4 address to a MAC address on a local network segment.
ndp: Neighbor Discovery Protocol: the IPv6 equivalent of ARP plus router discovery, using ICMPv6 messages.
http: Hypertext Transfer Protocol: the application-layer protocol used for transmitting web pages and other resources.
https: HTTP Secure: HTTP layered over TLS, providing encryption and authentication between client and server.
tls: Transport Layer Security: cryptographic protocol that provides secure communication over a network; successor to SSL.
ssl: Secure Sockets Layer: the deprecated predecessor to TLS. Should not be used for new deployments.
ftp: File Transfer Protocol: a standard network protocol used for transferring files between a client and server on a computer network.
sftp: SSH File Transfer Protocol: a secure file transfer protocol that runs over SSH, unlike plain FTP.
scp: Secure Copy Protocol: a means of securely transferring files between a local and remote host over SSH.
rsync: A utility for efficiently transferring and synchronizing files across systems by only copying the differences.
smtp: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol: the standard protocol for sending email between servers.
imap: Internet Message Access Protocol: a protocol for retrieving email from a server while keeping it on the server.
pop3: Post Office Protocol version 3: an older email retrieval protocol that typically downloads and deletes messages from the server.
bgp: Border Gateway Protocol: the routing protocol that exchanges routing information between autonomous systems on the internet.
ospf: Open Shortest Path First: a link-state interior gateway routing protocol for IP networks.
rip: Routing Information Protocol: a distance-vector routing protocol that uses hop count as its metric.
mpls: Multiprotocol Label Switching: a routing technique that directs data based on short path labels rather than long network addresses.
vpn: Virtual Private Network: extends a private network across a public one, providing encryption and anonymity.
ipsec: Internet Protocol Security: a suite of protocols for authenticating and encrypting IP packets, often used in VPNs.
wireguard: A modern, high-performance VPN protocol built into the Linux kernel.
openvpn: An open-source VPN implementation using SSL/TLS for key exchange.
mtu: Maximum Transmission Unit: the largest packet size that can be transmitted over a network link without fragmentation.
ttl: Time To Live: a field in IP packets that is decremented at each hop; when it reaches zero the packet is dropped.
cidr: Classless Inter-Domain Routing: a method for allocating IP addresses and routing that uses variable-length subnet masks.
subnet mask: A 32-bit number that separates the network portion of an IP address from the host portion.
mac address: Media Access Control address: a unique 48-bit identifier assigned to a network interface controller.
eui-64: Extended Unique Identifier: a 64-bit identifier derived from a MAC address, used to form the interface identifier of an IPv6 address.
loopback: A special network address (127.0.0.1 in IPv4, ::1 in IPv6) that refers to the local machine.
multicast: A one-to-many communication pattern where data is sent to a group of interested receivers.
anycast: A one-to-nearest communication pattern where data is delivered to the topologically closest member of a group.
unicast: A one-to-one communication pattern where data is sent to a single destination.
broadcast: A one-to-all communication pattern in a network segment. IPv6 has no broadcast; it uses multicast instead.
ethernet: The dominant family of wired LAN technologies, defined by IEEE 802.3, carrying frames over twisted pair, coax, or fiber.
osi model: A conceptual framework that standardizes network communication into seven layers, from physical media to applications.
tcp/ip model: A four-layer networking model (Link, Internet, Transport, Application) that underlies the modern internet.
latency: The time delay between sending a request and receiving a response, typically measured in milliseconds.
bandwidth: The maximum rate of data transfer across a network path, typically measured in bits per second.
throughput: The actual rate of successful data delivery over a network, often lower than the theoretical bandwidth.
packet: A formatted unit of data carried by a packet-switched network, containing headers and a payload.
frame: A data unit at the link layer, encapsulating a packet with link-layer addressing and error checking.
port: A 16-bit number identifying a specific process or service on a host, used with TCP or UDP.
port forwarding: A NAT technique that redirects incoming traffic on a specific port to a host inside a private network.
dmz: Demilitarized Zone: a subnetwork that exposes external-facing services to an untrusted network while isolating the internal network.
proxy: An intermediary server that forwards requests between clients and other servers.
reverse proxy: A proxy that sits in front of servers and forwards client requests to them, often for load balancing or TLS termination.
load balancer: A device or service that distributes incoming traffic across multiple backend servers.
cdn: Content Delivery Network: a geographically distributed network of servers that delivers content closer to users.
acl: Access Control List: a list of rules that specify which users or systems are granted or denied access to a resource.
aaa: Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting: the three pillars of access control in networking and security.
tls handshake: The initial negotiation in a TLS session where client and server agree on cipher suites and exchange keys.
dns record: An entry in a DNS zone file, such as A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, or TXT, that maps names to values.
a record: A DNS record that maps a domain name to an IPv4 address.
aaaa record: A DNS record that maps a domain name to an IPv6 address.
cname: Canonical Name record: a DNS record that aliases one domain name to another.
mx record: Mail Exchange record: a DNS record that specifies the mail servers for a domain.
txt record: A DNS record that holds arbitrary text, commonly used for SPF, DKIM, and domain verification.
spf: Sender Policy Framework: a DNS TXT record that lists servers authorized to send email for a domain.
dkim: DomainKeys Identified Mail: a method for signing email to verify authenticity.
dmarc: Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance: a policy that builds on SPF and DKIM to protect against email spoofing.
IPv4: Internet Protocol version 4: the fourth version of the Internet Protocol, using 32-bit addresses written in dotted-decimal notation (e.g., 192.168.1.1). Still the most widely deployed addressing scheme.
IPv6: Internet Protocol version 6: the successor to IPv4, using 128-bit addresses written in hexadecimal groups separated by colons. Designed to eliminate address exhaustion and restore end-to-end connectivity.
32-bit: A group of 32 binary digits. IPv4 addresses are 32 bits long.
32bit: An alternate spelling of 32-bit; it describes a value made of 32 binary digits.
32 bit: A group of 32 binary digits. IPv4 addresses are 32 bits long.
32-bit address: An IPv4 address containing 32 bits, commonly written as four decimal octets.
32-Bit-Adresse: An IPv4 address containing 32 bits, commonly written as four decimal octets.
32-bit addresses: IPv4 addresses containing 32 bits, commonly written as four decimal octets.
32-Bit-Adressen: IPv4 addresses containing 32 bits, commonly written as four decimal octets.
64-bit: A value made of 64 binary digits; common in modern CPU and operating-system architectures.
64 bit: A value made of 64 binary digits; common in modern CPU and operating-system architectures.
128-bit: A value made of 128 binary digits. IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long.
128 bit: A value made of 128 binary digits. IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long.
128-bit address: An IPv6 address containing 128 bits, written as eight hexadecimal groups.
128-Bit-Adresse: An IPv6 address containing 128 bits, written as eight hexadecimal groups.
8-bit: A group of eight binary digits, also called one byte or one octet in networking.
16-bit: A value made of 16 binary digits; TCP and UDP port numbers are 16 bits.
octet: A group of eight bits. IPv4 addresses are divided into four octets.
octets: Groups of eight bits. IPv4 addresses contain four octets.
Oktett: Eine Gruppe aus acht Bit. IPv4-Adressen werden in vier Oktette aufgeteilt.
Oktette: Gruppen aus jeweils acht Bit. IPv4-Adressen bestehen aus vier Oktetten.
dotted-decimal notation: The IPv4 format that writes four decimal octets separated by dots, such as 192.168.1.1.
dotted decimal notation: The IPv4 format that writes four decimal octets separated by dots.
punktierte Dezimalschreibweise: IPv4-Schreibweise mit vier durch Punkte getrennten Dezimal-Oktetten, zum Beispiel 192.168.1.1.
hexadecimal notation: A base-16 number format using digits 0-9 and letters A-F; IPv6 addresses use it.
hexadezimale Notation: Zahlenformat zur Basis 16 mit den Ziffern 0-9 und den Buchstaben A-F; IPv6-Adressen verwenden es.
address space: The complete set of addresses available in a numbering system, such as all possible IPv4 addresses.
Adressraum: Die Gesamtheit aller möglichen Adressen eines Nummernsystems, zum Beispiel aller IPv4-Adressen.
address exhaustion: The point at which a numbering system has no unallocated addresses left; IPv4 exhaustion helped drive IPv6 adoption.
Adressknappheit: Der Zustand, in dem keine Adressen eines Nummernsystems mehr frei sind; IPv4-Knappheit förderte die Einführung von IPv6.
address class: An older way of dividing IPv4 addresses into fixed network ranges, such as Class A, B, or C.
address classes: An older way of dividing IPv4 addresses into fixed network ranges, such as Class A, B, or C.
Adressklasse: Ältere Einteilung von IPv4-Adressen in feste Netzwerkbereiche, etwa Klasse A, B oder C.
Adressklassen: Ältere Einteilung von IPv4-Adressen in feste Netzwerkbereiche, etwa Klasse A, B oder C.
best-effort: A delivery model that tries to forward packets but does not guarantee delivery, order, or timing.
Best-Effort-Zustellung: A delivery model that tries to forward packets but does not guarantee delivery, order, or timing.
connectionless: Communication that sends packets without first establishing a dedicated connection between endpoints.
verbindungslos: Kommunikation, bei der Pakete ohne vorherigen Verbindungsaufbau zwischen den Endpunkten gesendet werden.
network prefix: The leading bits of an IP address that identify the network portion; its length is written after a slash, as in /24.
Netzwerkpräfix: Die führenden Bits einer IP-Adresse, die das Netzwerk kennzeichnen; die Länge steht nach einem Schrägstrich, etwa /24.
interface identifier: The part of an IPv6 address that identifies an interface within its subnet, often the lower 64 bits.
Interface-Identifier: Der Teil einer IPv6-Adresse, der eine Schnittstelle innerhalb ihres Subnetzes kennzeichnet, häufig die unteren 64 Bit.
IPv4 header: The control information at the start of an IPv4 packet, including source, destination, and TTL.
IPv4-Header: Steuerdaten am Anfang eines IPv4-Pakets, darunter Quelle, Ziel und TTL.
IPv6 header: The control information at the start of an IPv6 packet, including source, destination, and hop limit.
IPv6-Header: Steuerdaten am Anfang eines IPv6-Pakets, darunter Quelle, Ziel und Hop-Limit.
extension header: An optional IPv6 header placed after the main header to carry features such as routing or fragmentation information.
extension headers: Optional IPv6 headers placed after the main header to carry extra packet information.
Extension-Header: Optionaler IPv6-Header nach dem Haupteintrag, der zusätzliche Paketinformationen enthält.
fragmentation: Splitting a packet into smaller pieces so it can cross a link with a smaller MTU.
Fragmentierung: Aufteilen eines Pakets in kleinere Teile, damit es eine Verbindung mit kleinerer MTU passieren kann.
router advertisement: An ICMPv6 message by which a router announces network prefixes and configuration options to IPv6 hosts.
router advertisements: ICMPv6 messages by which routers announce network prefixes and configuration options to IPv6 hosts.
privacy extensions: IPv6 features that use temporary interface identifiers to make long-term device tracking harder.
autoconfiguration: Automatic setup of network settings, such as an IPv6 address generated from router advertisements.
Autokonfiguration: Automatische Einrichtung von Netzwerkeinstellungen, etwa einer IPv6-Adresse anhand von Router Advertisements.
transition mechanism: A technique that allows IPv4 and IPv6 networks to coexist or communicate during migration.
Übergangsmechanismus: Technik, mit der IPv4- und IPv6-Netze während einer Umstellung nebeneinander bestehen oder kommunizieren können.
end-to-end connectivity: Direct communication between two endpoints across intervening networks without translation breaking the connection.
Ende-zu-Ende-Konnektivität: Direkte Kommunikation zwischen zwei Endpunkten über zwischengeschaltete Netze hinweg, ohne dass Übersetzung die Verbindung unterbricht.
global unicast: An IPv6 address type intended to be globally unique and routable across the public internet.
link-local: An address usable only on the local network link; it is not routed beyond that link.
link-local address: An address usable only on the local network link; it is not routed beyond that link.
Link-Local-Adresse: Adresse, die nur auf der lokalen Netzwerkverbindung gilt und nicht darüber hinaus geroutet wird.
unique local address: An IPv6 address for private communication within an organization; it is not globally routed.
Unique-Local-Adresse: IPv6-Adresse für private Kommunikation innerhalb einer Organisation; sie wird nicht global geroutet.
unspecified address: An all-zero IP address used to indicate that a host has no assigned address or as an unspecified source.
loopback address: An address that sends traffic back to the same device, such as 127.0.0.1 or ::1.
broadcast address: An IPv4 destination address that delivers a packet to all hosts on a subnet.
multicast address: An address for sending packets to a group of subscribed interfaces rather than one host or every host.
Multicast-Adresse: Adresse zum Senden von Paketen an eine Gruppe ausgewählter Schnittstellen statt an einen oder alle Hosts.
static NAT: A fixed one-to-one mapping between a private IP address and a public IP address.
Statisches NAT: Feste Eins-zu-eins-Zuordnung zwischen einer privaten und einer öffentlichen IP-Adresse.
dynamic NAT: A temporary mapping from private addresses to a pool of public addresses, allocated as connections are made.
Dynamisches NAT: Zeitweilige Zuordnung privater Adressen zu einem Pool öffentlicher Adressen, die bei Verbindungen vergeben werden.
private ranges: IPv4 address blocks reserved for private networks and not routed directly on the public internet.
private IPv4 address: An IPv4 address from a range reserved for private networks.
private IP address: An IP address used inside a private network and not directly routed on the public internet.
public IP address: An IP address that can be routed across the public internet.
public IPv4 address: An IPv4 address that can be routed across the public internet.
CIDR notation: The address-and-prefix format, such as 192.168.1.0/24, used to describe an IP network.
CIDR-Notation: Adress- und Präfixschreibweise wie 192.168.1.0/24 zur Beschreibung eines IP-Netzwerks.
subnetting: Dividing an IP network into smaller networks by borrowing bits from the host portion of an address.
subnet masks: Values that distinguish the network bits from the host bits in an IPv4 address.
address compression: Shortening an IPv6 address by omitting leading zeroes in groups and replacing one zero run with ::.
hex digit: One symbol in base-16 notation: a digit from 0 to 9 or a letter from A to F.
prefix length: The number of leading address bits that identify a network, written after a slash in CIDR notation.
protocol: A set of rules that defines how devices format, send, and interpret network messages.
Internet Protocol: The network-layer protocol that addresses and routes packets between networks.
IP packet: A unit of data carried by IP, consisting of a header and its payload.
header: Control information placed before data so a protocol can deliver or process it.
header field: A named value in a packet header that controls or describes packet handling.
payload: The data carried by a packet after its protocol headers.
IHL: Internet Header Length: the IPv4 header size, measured in 32-bit words.
Internet Header Length: The IPv4 header-length field, measured in 32-bit words.
total length: The IPv4 field giving the size of the complete packet, including header and payload.
source address: The IP address of the device that sent a packet.
destination address: The IP address of the device to which a packet is sent.
source port: The transport-layer port identifying the sending application or connection.
destination port: The transport-layer port identifying the receiving application or service.
private source IP: The private IP address a device uses before a router translates it for internet access.
public IP: An IP address that can be routed on the public internet.
network portion: The bits of an IP address that identify its network, as determined by the prefix or mask.
host portion: The bits of an IP address that identify a device within its network.
host address: The part or value of an IP address used to identify a device within a network.
network address: The address that identifies a subnet itself; host bits are set to zero.
usable host: A device address within a subnet that is available for assignment, excluding reserved addresses.
Class A: A historical IPv4 class with a large network range, identified by a leading zero bit.
Class B: A historical IPv4 class identified by the leading bit pattern 10.
Class C: A historical IPv4 class identified by the leading bit pattern 110.
Class D: The historical IPv4 range reserved for multicast traffic.
Class E: The historical IPv4 range reserved for experimental or future use.
Klasse A: Historische IPv4-Klasse mit großem Netzwerkbereich, erkennbar am führenden Null-Bit.
Klasse B: Historische IPv4-Klasse, erkennbar am führenden Bitmuster 10.
Klasse C: Historische IPv4-Klasse, erkennbar am führenden Bitmuster 110.
Klasse E: Historischer IPv4-Bereich für experimentelle oder zukünftige Nutzung.
reserved address: An IP address or range set aside for a special purpose and not assigned for ordinary host use.
limited broadcast: The IPv4 address 255.255.255.255, used to reach hosts on the local network.
APIPA: Automatic Private IP Addressing: link-local IPv4 addressing, commonly in 169.254.0.0/16, when normal configuration fails.
address pool: A set of addresses a service or router can assign to devices or connections.
translation table: A router table that records address and port changes made by NAT so replies can be sent back correctly.
mapping table: A table that records which translated address or port belongs to each internal connection.
port mapping: The association between an external port and an internal device or service port.
outbound request: A request initiated by a device on a local network and sent toward an external service.
inbound response: A reply arriving from an external service for a connection initiated inside the network.
NAT overload: A form of PAT that lets many private devices share one public IPv4 address by using distinct ports.
Paket-Header: Steuerinformationen vor den Nutzdaten, die deren Zustellung oder Verarbeitung ermöglichen.
Nutzdaten: Die Daten eines Pakets nach den Protokoll-Headern.
Quelladresse: IP-Adresse des Geräts, das ein Paket gesendet hat.
Zieladresse: IP-Adresse des Geräts, an das ein Paket gesendet wird.
Quellport: Port der Transportschicht, der die sendende Anwendung oder Verbindung identifiziert.
Zielport: Port der Transportschicht, der die empfangende Anwendung oder den Dienst identifiziert.
Netzwerkanteil: Die Bits einer IP-Adresse, die anhand von Präfix oder Maske das Netzwerk kennzeichnen.
Hostanteil: Die Bits einer IP-Adresse, die ein Gerät innerhalb seines Netzwerks kennzeichnen.
Netzwerkadresse: Adresse zur Kennzeichnung eines Subnetzes; die Host-Bits sind auf null gesetzt.
Hostadresse: IP-Adresse zur Kennzeichnung eines Geräts innerhalb eines Netzwerks.
reservierte Adresse: IP-Adresse oder Bereich für einen besonderen Zweck, nicht zur normalen Host-Zuweisung.
Adresspool: Adressmenge, die ein Dienst oder Router Geräten oder Verbindungen zuweisen kann.
Übersetzungstabelle: Routertabelle mit NAT-Adress- und Portänderungen, damit Antworten korrekt zurückgesendet werden.
Zuordnungstabelle: Tabelle, die festhält, welche übersetzte Adresse oder welcher Port zu einer internen Verbindung gehört.
Portzuordnung: Zuordnung eines externen Ports zu einem internen Gerät oder Dienst-Port.
ausgehende Anfrage: Von einem Gerät im lokalen Netzwerk gestartete Anfrage an einen externen Dienst.
eingehende Antwort: Antwort eines externen Dienstes auf eine innerhalb des Netzwerks gestartete Verbindung.
traffic class: The IPv6 header field used to mark packet priority and traffic handling, including QoS information.
flow label: An IPv6 header field that marks packets belonging to the same traffic flow.
payload length: The IPv6 header field giving the number of payload bytes after the fixed header.
next header: The IPv6 field identifying the next protocol header, such as TCP or an extension header.
hop limit: The IPv6 field decremented by each router; the packet is discarded when it reaches zero.
header checksum: A value used to detect errors in a packet header; IPv4 has one, while IPv6 does not.
path MTU: The smallest MTU among all links along a route between a sender and receiver.
path MTU discovery: A process that determines the largest packet size that can travel along a route without fragmentation.
PMTUD: Path MTU Discovery: the process of finding the packet-size limit along a network route.
QoS: Quality of Service: techniques for prioritizing or managing different kinds of network traffic.
Quality of Service: Techniques for prioritizing or managing different kinds of network traffic.
Klasse: Historische IPv4-Gruppe mit festgelegtem Adressbereich, etwa A, B, C, D oder E.
Fragment Offset: An IPv4 header field that indicates where a fragment belongs in the original packet.
Identification field: An IPv4 header value used to identify fragments that belong to the same original packet.
Flags field: IPv4 header bits that control or indicate fragmentation behavior.
reassembly: Recombining packet fragments into the original packet at the receiving device.
header length: The size of a protocol header, which may be fixed or encoded in a header field.
Hop-by-Hop Options: An IPv6 extension header containing information that must be examined by each router along the path.
Destination Options: An IPv6 extension header carrying options for the packet destination.
Routing Header: An IPv6 extension header that carries routing information for the packet path.
Fragment Header: An IPv6 extension header used by the source to describe packet fragments.
